nodes.statement: The framework applies only when authoring is version-controlled, claims are propositional, audience schemas diverge, and artifact volume exceeds human verification capacity.
nodes.span: authoring is version-controlled (C1); claims are propositional rather than purely narrative (C2); audience-schema divergence is non-trivial (C3)
nodes.status_reason: The boundary conditions can be checked as stated but do not follow from earlier nodes or the reader's held terms.

nodes.statement: Generative AI introduces a cost asymmetry where verifying the structural substrate is sub-linear in cost, while verifying the prose rendering is super-linear.
nodes.span: AI verification cost on the spine scales sub-linearly with claim volume while verification cost on the rendering scales super-linearly with token count.
nodes.status_reason: Relies on formal mathematical scaling functions and parameters that the reader model explicitly does not hold.

nodes.statement: The Operator role must be split into structural-substrate operations performed by AI and judgment operations performed by humans.
nodes.span: The Operator's intrinsic operations split into two classes with qualitatively different projection patterns.
nodes.status_reason: Derived from the cost asymmetry which makes this division of labor economically dominant.

nodes.statement: The structural substrate and the prose rendering of a knowledge artifact can be optimized independently of one another.
nodes.span: Meaning and meaningfulness are separately optimizable: $\sigma : L \to S$ without consulting any R
nodes.status_reason: Relies on the formal extraction operator sigma stated in symbols, which the reader model does not hold.

nodes.statement: Two different prose renderings of the same structural substrate will reach the same conclusions as long as both preserve the underlying structural elements.
nodes.span: two prose renderings of the same spine arrive at the same set of conclusions iff both renderings preserve the spine's structural elements.
nodes.status_reason: Derived as a preservation result from the faithful extraction axiom.

nodes.statement: A faithful extraction operator can successfully recover the locked structural elements of a spine from its rendering.
nodes.span: when a rendering preserves the locked elements of the spine, the $\sigma$ extraction operator recovers them.
nodes.status_reason: Assumes the existence and reliability of the formal sigma extraction operator not held by the reader.

nodes.statement: Organizations that publish the structural substrate of their work achieve higher rates of knowledge recombination than those that only publish prose.
nodes.span: Organizations that publish the substrate of their knowledge artifacts as a first-class artifact achieve higher rates of knowledge recombination
nodes.status_reason: Derived from the sub-linear cost of AI querying the published substrate.

nodes.statement: The Eisenhardt & Martin and Zollo & Winter papers on dynamic capabilities yield the same underlying substrate propositions despite using different vocabularies.
nodes.span: The two formalisms yield the same substrate proposition: dynamic capabilities exist as a separable construct above operating routines.
nodes.status_reason: Can be checked against the historical record of the cited management papers.

nodes.statement: The Kulkarni et al. paper demonstrates independent authors arriving at the same underlying substrate propositions through different prose renderings.
nodes.span: independent operators arriving at the same underlying substrate through different rendering choices.
nodes.status_reason: Can be checked against the text of the Kulkarni et al. paper.

nodes.statement: Organizations should govern and publish the structural substrate of their knowledge artifacts as a primary asset alongside the prose renderings.
nodes.span: publish the substrate of their knowledge artifacts as a first-class governed asset alongside renderings.
nodes.status_reason: Derived from the recombination and verification capacity advantages of queryable substrates.

nodes.statement: Organizations should redesign roles and incentives to reflect the partition between structural-substrate operations and judgment operations.
nodes.span: redesign Operator roles around the structural-substrate / judgment partition rather than around the legacy task-level workflow.
nodes.status_reason: Derived from the cost asymmetry that makes the substrate-judgment partition economically dominant.

nodes.statement: Academic peer review should evaluate the coherence of the structural substrate separately from the craft of the prose rendering.
nodes.span: evaluate substrate coherence and prose craft as separate inputs rather than as a single rolled-up review verdict.
nodes.status_reason: Derived from the cost asymmetry which makes substrate review cheap for AI but prose review expensive for humans.
